newsitem.title: ALBANIA: United States sends military adviser to Albania.
newsitem.headline: United States sends military adviser to Albania.

text.p: The United States has sent a permanent military envoy to Albania to demonstrate the close cooperation between the two countries, an Albanian government spokesman said on Wednesday.
Defence ministry spokesman Pandeli Ristani told Reuters Colonel Karl F. Knabe II had been seconded to Albania as military adviser to Defence Minister Safet Zhulali for a six month period.
Knabe, a Vietnam war veteran, is the second U.S. adviser to be sent to the Balkan country since 1995.

Knabe has 30 years of experience in organising military exercises, conducting international negotiations and selling military equipment. He was a chief negotiator in Europe for NATO arms control in the late 1980s.
"His arrival speaks of close relations existing between our two countries," Ristani said, noting that the two countries held four bilateral exercises last year.
Washington said last year it would make available more than $100 million for military training, equipping peacekeeping units and joint exercises in Albania.

Ristani said Albania, which has been modernising its defences to reach the required technical standards for NATO membership, had already accumulated a substantial amount of transport and communication equipment.
Albania has an army of 60,000 men, including 20,000 conscripts, a 2,500-strong navy and an air force of 10,000.

The Balkan nation was among the first countries three years ago to join NATO's Partnership for Peace programme. It has conducted 24 joint military exercises with NATO and other countries in the past two years.
Despite cordial relations with Albania, the United States criticised the conduct of Albania's general election last May and advised President Sali Berisha to call a fresh poll as soon as possible.
